title: Skriv kravspecifikationen för ett nytt skydd vid ett transportband
person: A design engineer at a Swedish packaging maker writing the requirements for a new conveyor guard to send out for quotes.
review: The guard covers the in-running nips at both end drums, takes 1 kN without permanent deformation, mesh openings at most 20 mm at least 120 mm from the drum, an interlocked hatch stated positively, an opening force of at most 150 N (not 15 kg), at most 12 kg per section, RAL 1023, washable at 80 °C and 100 bar; the 2 s stopping time is a TBR for Jonas Berglund by 15 November 2026.
revised_review: The belt stands still within 1 s of the hatch opening, the stopping-time TBR is closed, and an emergency stop button on each side is a new requirement; nothing else changed.

criteria.text: Every mechanical check in run.py passes for this stage.
Every requirement has an id of its own, used once.
Requirements say shall, facts will and goals should; nothing says must.
No vague word from the notes survives into a requirement.
Every TBD or TBR has an owner and a date.
Every requirement names test, analysis, inspection or demonstration.
Every value has a space before its unit symbol, °C and % included.
The notes' unit spellings are replaced by the SI symbols.
The interlock is a positive requirement (the hatch stays locked until the belt has stopped), not a list of what must not happen.
The opening force is given in newtons (150 N), not as a mass in kilograms.
The specification makes no claim that the guard is certified or compliant with a directive or standard.
The stopping time is 1 s with no TBR left for it, and the emergency stops are a new requirement with its own id.

source: Synthetic material created for this evaluation pack; the companies, schools and people are invented.
